classes.name: RiskAssessment
comment: Composite judgment of technical strength and litigation exposure.

classes.name: CaseLaw
comment: A structured judicial decision - captured as reasoning, not just judgment text.

classes.name: Transaction
comment: The commercial or corporate event giving rise to potential tax consequences.

classes.name: FirmOpinion
comment: A formal KPMG tax opinion - facts through recommendation, in one record.

classes.name: PartyAttribute
comment: A qualifying attribute of a Party that determines which provisions apply.

classes.name: ClientEngagementDocument
comment: Engagement deliverable embedding a real fact pattern and a position.

classes.name: KnowledgeRepositoryItem
comment: Curated, anonymised position paper maintained by Knowledge Management / DPP.

classes.name: AdvanceRuling
comment: A pre-transaction determination; persuasive but not universally binding.

classes.name: RulingAuthority
comment: An institution empowered to issue advance rulings (direct-tax or GST). Split out from AdvanceRuling (a document class) and from JudicialForum (case-deciding institutions) because a ruling authority is neither - it is a distinct institution type with its own bindingness rules. Added per Indian_Tax_SLM_Research_Report.md Section 4.2 defect #3.

classes.name: JudicialForum
comment: Enumerated hierarchy establishing binding vs. persuasive weight of a case.

classes.name: InternationalGuidance
comment: Non-binding but persuasive international interpretive material.

classes.name: ComplianceForm
comment: A prescribed filing instrument tied to a provision or transaction.

classes.name: Recommendation
comment: The practical next step flowing from the conclusion.

classes.name: StatutoryProvision
comment: Binding primary law enacted by the legislature.

classes.name: TaxTreaty
comment: Bilateral/multilateral agreement that can override domestic law for a cross-border fact pattern.

classes.name: Issue
comment: The specific question framed for analysis.

classes.name: Industry
comment: Sector context that shapes issue framing and risk tolerance.

classes.name: LegalProposition
comment: A reified legal claim/interpretation - claim text, applicability conditions, supporting and opposing authorities (with role), jurisdiction, statute regime, confidence and status (settled/contested/superseded) - kept separate from the documents (CaseLaw, FirmOpinion) that assert it, so qualified and conflicting views can coexist and be queried. Added per Indian_Tax_SLM_Research_Report.md Section 4.3(a).

classes.name: Conclusion
comment: The final technical position reached.

classes.name: LegalEvent
comment: A dated legal event (amendment, overruling, reversal, supersession, withdrawal, stay) with the instrument that caused it and its scope - lets OVERRULES/SUPERSEDED_BY/WITHDRAWN_BY/AMENDED_BY/STAYED_BY-type relationships be queried with 'when' and 'by what instrument', which a bare triple cannot express. Added per Indian_Tax_SLM_Research_Report.md Section 4.2 defect #10 / Section 4.3(b).

classes.name: CaseCitation
comment: The formal citation record for a case-law decision (reporter, volume, page, year - e.g. '(2021) 3 SCC 1'). Kept separate from CaseLaw's 'citation' text field so multiple parallel citations for the same case, or citations shared/cross-referenced across cases, can be their own node. Added while incorporating gaps flagged by the 11_extract_case_law.py extraction run.

classes.name: ControlledVocabulary
comment: Fixed enumerations used as attribute values across the classes above, so downstream filtering and risk-weighting stay consistent (Section 6 of the conceptual ontology document).

classes.name: TaxTopic
comment: A controlled classification tag used to categorize case law, issues and firm opinions by subject area.

classes.name: DelegatedLegislation
comment: Subordinate instrument issued under statutory authority to implement, clarify or operationalise a provision.

classes.name: PenaltyExposure
comment: The statutory consequence of non-compliance or an adverse position.

classes.name: TechnicalAlert
comment: Time-stamped commentary tracking a legal change and its impact on positions.

classes.name: Party
comment: An entity or person who is the subject of the tax analysis.

classes.name: HSNSACCode
comment: A Harmonized System of Nomenclature / Services Accounting Code used for GST classification. Added per Indian_Tax_SLM_Research_Report.md Section 4.2 defect #12 (GST substructure).

classes.name: GSTRateEntry
comment: A GST rate applicable to an HSN/SAC code for a given effective period - the deterministic rate-table target the research report recommends routing all rate lookups to (never generate a rate). Added per Indian_Tax_SLM_Research_Report.md Section 4.2 defect #12.

classes.name: DeliverableOutput
comment: The client-facing artifact produced once analysis is complete.

classes.name: RevenuePosition
comment: The tax department's actual or likely stance on an issue.

classes.name: TrainingMaterial
comment: National-office material used for internal knowledge transfer.

classes.name: LitigationProcessStage
comment: A stage in the dispute-resolution pathway.

classes.name: TechnicalDiscussion
comment: Non-binding policy deliberation that still informs interpretation.

classes.name: HighCourtStage
comment: A litigation-process stage at the High Court (distinct from the HighCourt JudicialForum institution class - link the two via HAS_FORUM). Renamed from the collision-suffixed 'HighCourt_2' per Indian_Tax_SLM_Research_Report.md Section 4.2 defect #1.

classes.name: SupremeCourtStage
comment: A litigation-process stage at the Supreme Court (distinct from the SupremeCourt JudicialForum institution class - link the two via HAS_FORUM). Renamed from the collision-suffixed 'SupremeCourt_2' per Indian_Tax_SLM_Research_Report.md Section 4.2 defect #1.

classes.name: Argument
comment: A position advanced on an issue, for or against the taxpayer.

classes.name: TreatyNotification
comment: A notification that gives effect to a tax treaty (e.g. Notification No. 68/2019 adopting the India-Hong Kong DTAA) - modelled once, as a Notification, not duplicated under TaxTreaty. Deduped per Indian_Tax_SLM_Research_Report.md Section 4.2 defect #2.

classes.name: StateJurisdiction
comment: An Indian state or union territory, for SGST divergence and state-level GST AAR/AAAR jurisdiction. Subclass of the existing Jurisdiction placeholder class (itself still flagged open - see Section 9 of the conceptual ontology document / prior chat history). Added per Indian_Tax_SLM_Research_Report.md Section 4.2 defect #12.

classes.name: FactPattern
comment: An anonymised, reusable scenario extracted from historical engagements.
Composite class: a fact pattern is made up of a Party, a Transaction, a Jurisdiction and an Issue (see the involvesParty / involvesTransaction / raises relationships).

classes.name: Layer_FirmIntellectualCapital
comment: Where the firm's proprietary value sits; the SME notes flag this as the single most important source layer for the KG build.

classes.name: Layer_JudicialInternationalInterpretiveAuthority
comment: The most heavily weighted interpretive layer per the SME notes.

classes.name: Layer_OpinionGeneration
comment: Mostly derived at analysis time rather than sourced from a document; this is the layer specific to opinion generation itself.

classes.name: Jurisdiction
comment: Referenced by relationship domain/range in the source ontology but not yet one of the formal top-level classes - flagged for SME confirmation (Section 9 of the conceptual ontology document).

classes.name: Layer_FactsLayer
comment: Marked "critical" in the SME notes: most opinions are generated from facts, not from law in the abstract.

classes.name: Layer_PrimarySourcesOfAuthority
comment: The foundation layer; binding law that nothing else can override except by amendment or a superior source.

classes.name: LegalConcept
comment: A general legal principle or proposition of law (e.g. 'the proviso to Section 47(iv) applies only when the transferee company is 100% Indian-owned'), distinct from any single case - multiple cases can instantiate/apply the same concept. Added while incorporating gaps flagged by the 11_extract_case_law.py extraction run; complements (does not replace) CaseLaw's existing ratioDecidendi/holding data properties, which stay as the case-specific text.

classes.name: Layer_Output
comment: Named in the SME's own "Suggested Final Knowledge Graph Structure" as OUTPUT but not separately numbered as a level in the source notes.

classes.name: SlumpSale
comment: Lump-sum transfer of an undertaking without assigning values to individual assets (ITA 1961 §2(42C) / ITA 2025 §2(103)).

object_properties.name: INTERPRETS
comment: Edge property `relation_type` (values: 'interpreted'/'applied'/'referred'/'raises_issue') disambiguates sections_interpreted vs sections_applied vs sections_referred vs an Issue this case raised - all collapse onto this one relationship type since the ontology has no separate APPLIES/REFERS_TO property for CaseLaw->StatutoryProvision. Also carries `cited_as` (the raw citation text, e.g. '9(1)(vi)') and `act` (which Act the extraction said the citation was under, if stated). Populated by extract_case_law.py; this schema (an OWL-derived JSON with no native way to declare data properties ON an object property/relationship) documents it here as a comment rather than a formal declaration - was previously undocumented entirely.

object_properties.name: OVERRIDES
comment: 2026-08-28: EXTENDED. Was TaxTreaty->StatutoryProvision only, no inverse - domain/range broadened to also
cover Circular->Circular and StatutoryProvision->StatutoryProvision precedence (e.g. a later Circular
clarifying/overriding an earlier one), and OVERRIDDEN_BY added as the queryable inverse. Legal
PRECEDENCE, not amendment/supersession (SUPERSEDED_BY already covers that). Domain covers Act via
StatutoryProvision (Act is its subclass, same convention PART_OF already uses). ALWAYS conditional in
practice (sec 90(2) treaty override only applies where more beneficial to the assessee; GAAR/PPT can in
turn limit a treaty benefit) - every OVERRIDES edge MUST carry an overrideCondition value stating that
condition; an edge with no condition text should be treated as a data-quality error, not an absolute
rule. Seeded narrowly and deterministically for well-established, black-letter structural rules (sec
90(2) DTAA-vs-Act) - NOT auto-generated by extraction, and NOT populated for case-specific precedence
questions without legal-domain review. See Graph_First_Retrieval_Design.md Section 2.2.

object_properties.name: CORRESPONDS_TO
comment: Cross-Act provision correspondence (e.g. Income-tax Act 1961 Section 90 (treaty override) CORRESPONDS_TO 2025 Act Section 159) - declared since early in this project but never populated by any converter until build_act_correspondence.py (added 2026-08-27; see Ontology_Legal_Review_2026-08-27.md). Edge properties: `basis` (how the mapping was derived, e.g. 'llm_text_comparison' or 'manual'), `confidence` (0-1).

object_properties.name: PART_OF
comment: Structural hierarchy: SubSection->Section, Clause->SubSection, SubClause->Clause, and (added 2026-08-27) top-level Section->Act, since Act is itself a StatutoryProvision subclass - previously top-level Sections had NO parent edge at all (Act was a declared-but-never-populated class). Populated by chunking.py; was used in code since early in this project but never declared here until now.

Extended (2026-08-27) to also cover Article->TaxTreaty: the ontology already declares Article as a TaxTreaty subclass (same shape as Section->Act) but had no relationship to attach an extracted treaty Article back to its parent TaxTreaty - same generic structural-hierarchy relation reused rather than declaring a redundant treaty-specific one. Populated by extract_treaty.py.

object_properties.name: IS_SUBSIDIARY_OF
comment: Ownership relationship for evaluating Section 47(iv) / ITA 2025 Sec 70(1)(c) corporate restructuring exemptions.

object_properties.name: TRIGGERS_DEFAULT
comment: Links failure of withholding/filing obligations to Section 201 assessee-in-default proceedings.

data_properties.name: stance
comment: 2026-08-28: NEW. Controlled vocabulary: 'taxpayer_favorable' | 'revenue_favorable' | 'mixed' | 'unknown'.
DERIVED DETERMINISTICALLY (not LLM-guessed) from the case's own issue_outcomes[].winner tally already
produced by extract_case_law.py's extraction prompt - same 'derive from already-extracted structured
fields, don't ask the model to self-report a second time' convention as forum_level/jurisdiction_scope
in that file. 'mixed' when issues split between assessee/revenue; 'unknown' when no issue_outcomes were
extracted - left unset rather than guessed, matching this project's existing convention of leaving a
field unset over guessing wrong (see derive_jurisdiction_scope()). Scoped to the case's overall outcome
across all its issues, not one one issue in isolation - see stanceBasis for the breakdown.

data_properties.name: stanceBasis
comment: Human-readable justification for `stance`, e.g. '2 issue(s) decided for assessee, 0 for revenue' - an audit trail so a retrieval/generation consumer (or a human reviewer) can see WHY a case was labeled a given stance, not just trust the label blindly.

data_properties.name: retrievalSummary
comment: 2026-08-28: NEW. Composed DETERMINISTICALLY from each finding's issue+holding+winner (already extracted
structured fields), NOT a fresh LLM-authored abstract - avoids the extraction-quality/recall risk flagged
in Graph_First_Retrieval_Design.md Section evaluating a metadata-only retrieval design (a thin or generic
LLM-written summary would degrade recall below what full chunk-text embedding gives today). This is the
text embedded into the new CaseLaw-level 'case_law_retrieval_index' vector index (see
framework/core/retrieve/case_law_entry_points.py) used to find ENTRY POINT nodes for graph traversal,
distinct from the existing Chunk-level embedding index used for the general hybrid pipeline.

data_properties.name: retrievalKeywords
comment: Comma-separated. Union of the case's own extracted keywords/legal_concepts plus cited section numbers and legal-principle short phrases - deterministically composed, not a new LLM call. Lets a question surface this case even when its caption/title shares no words with the question.

data_properties.name: sourceMdPath
comment: 2026-08-28: NEW. Absolute path to the converted .md file this entity was extracted from - see
md_hydration.py / Semantic_Graph_Retrieval_Architecture.md. Lets the 'semantic_graph' retrieval mode
read this entity's text LIVE from the source file at query time instead of only ever seeing whatever
was captured in a Chunk node at ingestion time. Stamped by attach_pipeline_metadata() (Act path) and
build_graph_from_extraction() (case-law path); Circular/TaxTreaty paths still need the same stamping
added as a mechanical follow-up (see the architecture doc's open-items section).

data_properties.name: overrideCondition
comment: Mandatory companion to every OVERRIDES edge - states WHEN the override applies (e.g. 'only if treaty provisions are more beneficial to the assessee, per sec 90(2) of the Income-tax Act'). See OVERRIDES's own comment.

data_properties.name: actName
comment: Human-readable Act name, e.g. 'Income-tax Act, 2025'.

data_properties.name: actYear
comment: Enactment year, e.g. 2025. Auto-detected from actName if not given explicitly - see extract_entities.py's --act-year.

data_properties.name: actNumber
comment: e.g. '30' for '[30 OF 2025]'. Optional.

data_properties.name: actNamespace
comment: The short id (e.g. 'ITA2025', 'ITA1961') this Act's node id equals, and that every Section/SubSection/Clause/SubClause id under it is prefixed with - see chunking.generate_entity_id()'s docstring (2026-08-27) for why a bare section NUMBER isn't a stable identity across more than one Act.

data_properties.name: precedential_value
comment: LLM-assessed importance/weight of this holding (e.g. 'landmark', 'leading case on X'). Already populated by extract_case_law.py from the extraction prompt's `importance` field; this entry formalizes it in the ontology - it was previously populated but undeclared.

data_properties.name: binding_scope
comment: LLM-assessed textual description of who/what this holding binds (e.g. 'binding on all Tribunals within the jurisdiction'). Already populated by extract_case_law.py; this entry formalizes it - it was previously populated but undeclared. Complements the deterministic jurisdiction_scope property below (LLM judgment vs. a structured territory lookup).

data_properties.name: jurisdiction_scope
comment: Deterministic (not LLM) territory a ruling binds within, derived from forum_level + court (e.g. Supreme Court -> 'All India'; Bombay High Court -> 'Maharashtra & Goa (Bombay High Court)') - see extract_case_law.derive_jurisdiction_scope(), added 2026-08-27. Previously the `jurisdiction` property was set to the raw court name verbatim, identical to `court` itself and carrying no extra information despite the name suggesting a distinct concept.

data_properties.name: residentialStatus
comment: Controlled vocabulary: 'RESIDENT' | 'NON_RESIDENT' | 'NOT_ORDINARILY_RESIDENT'.

data_properties.name: ownershipPercentage
comment: Percentage of shareholding held by parent entity (e.g. 100.0 for wholly owned subsidiary).
